title: Congenital Hypothyroidism: Newborn Screening, Levothyroxine Timing and Etiologies
subject: ss-paediatric-endocrinology
module: Thyroid Disorders, Short Stature and Skeletal Dysplasias

steps.say: Newborn blood spot screening for congenital hypothyroidism requires precise timing to avoid the physiologic surge immediately after birth.
steps.tx: Execute **Newborn screening sampling window** protocols between 48 and 72 hours of life on dried blood spots to evaluate thyroid-stimulating hormone. Sampling prior to 48 hours causes unacceptable false-positive recalls due to the physiological neonatal TSH surge that peaks at 30 minutes after delivery and gradually wanes over two days.

vis.alt: Clinical illustration of an infant with congenital hypothyroidism displaying macroglossia, abdominal distension with umbilical hernia, large fontanelle, and hypotonia.
vis.caption: Characteristic clinical features of congenital hypothyroidism in an infant.

steps.say: The etiological spectrum separates permanent congenital hypothyroidism into dysgenesis and autosomal recessive dyshormonogenesis.
steps.tx: Analyze the **Etiological distribution (dysgenesis vs dyshormonogenesis)** underlying permanent primary hypothyroidism in infants. Thyroid dysgenesis represents 85% of cases, comprising ectopia 60% (sublingual lingual thyroid), athyreosis 25% (total agenesis), and hypoplasia 5%. Autosomal recessive thyroid dyshormonogenesis accounts for the remaining 15% from enzymatic pathway defects.

vis.title: Etiological Breakdown of Congenital Hypothyroidism
rows: Failure of iodide organification and symporter

steps.say: Immediate replacement therapy with weight-adjusted oral levothyroxine is essential to protect normal neurocognitive development.
steps.tx: Initiate an **Initial levothyroxine dosing benchmark** of 10-15 mcg/kg/day orally as single daily dosing within the first two weeks of life. This full starting dose rapidly normalizes serum free T4 within 3-7 days and suppresses elevated TSH within 2-4 weeks, safeguarding neurocognitive potential and preventing irreversible IQ loss.

steps.say: Levothyroxine tablets must be crushed with breast milk or water, avoiding known dietary binders that block absorption.
steps.tx: Prevent drug interactions involving **Soy and iron interference with absorption** by educating parents on strict administration techniques. Levothyroxine tablets must be crushed in breast milk or water; co-administration with soy formulas, calcium carbonate, iron supplements, and aluminum hydroxide severely inhibits intestinal absorption, causing persistent TSH elevation.

left.title: Approved Administration
points: Crushed in small volume of breast milk or water
Administered via spoon or oral syringe immediately
Given on an empty stomach 30 minutes before feed

right.title: Absorption Inhibitors
points: Soy formulas chelate hormone in intestinal lumen
Calcium carbonate and sucralfate blunt bioavailability

steps.say: Close laboratory monitoring in infancy ensures hormonal targets remain in the optimal upper physiological range.
steps.tx: Maintain tight surveillance targeting the **Target serum free T4 monitoring range** during the initial year of therapy. During the first year of life, serum free T4 must be kept in the upper half of the age-specific reference range (1.4-2.3 ng/dL) with TSH normalized between 0.5 and 2.0 mIU/L.

vis.alt: Diagram of the hypothalamic-pituitary-thyroid axis showing thyrotropin-releasing hormone, thyroid-stimulating hormone regulation, negative feedback by free thyroxine, and peripheral conversion.
vis.caption: Hypothalamic-pituitary-thyroid axis and feedback regulation guiding levothyroxine dose titration.

steps.say: Transient hypothyroidism must be distinguished from permanent disease by identifying maternal and environmental triggers.
steps.tx: Recognize distinct **Transient congenital hypothyroidism triggers** causing temporary neonatal thyroid axis suppression. Common etiologies include maternal TSH receptor blocking antibodies (TRBAb) crossed transplacentally, maternal antithyroid drug ingestion (propylthiouracil, methimazole), endemic iodine deficiency, or excessive topical iodinated antiseptic exposure in preterm neonates inducing Wolff-Chaikoff block.

steps.say: In children with a normal gland in situ, a diagnostic withdrawal trial at three years of age establishes permanency.
steps.tx: Implement a formal **Trial off levothyroxine at age 3 years** to clarify permanent versus transient etiology. In children without documented thyroid ectopia or aplasia on infant scintigraphy or ultrasound, a trial off levothyroxine for 4-6 weeks at age 3 years assesses whether hypothyroidism is permanent or transient after brain myelination completes.

left.title: Indication Criteria
points: Child reaches age 3 years with complete CNS myelination
Normal thyroid gland visualized on neonatal ultrasound/radionuclide scan
No requirement for progressive dose escalation during early life

right.title: Re-evaluation Outcomes
points: Discontinue levothyroxine for 4-6 weeks under endocrine supervision
TSH elevation > 10 mIU/L confirms permanent hypothyroidism
Normal TSH and FT4 establishes transient disease recovery

steps.say: Pendred syndrome is an important genetic cause of dyshormonogenesis with associated sensorineural hearing loss.
steps.tx: Identify the characteristic **Pendred syndrome pairing** in children presenting with goitrous congenital hypothyroidism and hearing loss. Pendred syndrome is an autosomal recessive mutation in SLC26A4 encoding pendrin (an anion transporter in thyroid and inner ear), pairing congenital dyshormonogenic goitrous hypothyroidism with sensorineural hearing loss and enlarged vestibular aqueducts on imaging.

vis.title: Clinical Features of Pendred Syndrome
rows: Profound prelingual or progressive hearing impairment
Bony cochlear defect on high-resolution temporal CT
